name: primitives
title: Canvas primitives
summary: The five basic canvas shapes on a dark background: a filled rect, a stroked rounded rect, a filled circle, a stroked oval and a round-capped line.
prompt: Draw a filled rectangle, an outlined rounded rectangle, a circle, an oval and a thick line on a dark canvas.
teaches: Draw rect, roundRect, circle, oval and line commands in a canvas
Switch between filled and outlined shapes with the paint style fill or stroke
Set the colour and stroke width with a paint command before the shapes that use them
Give the canvas its background with a background modifier instead of a full-size drawRect
Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre

snippets.note: drawRect by its left, top, right, bottom edges
drawRoundRect with corner radii rx, ry
a stroke paint: style stroke, strokeWidth 4
only the changed keys: the stroke style carries over, width 6 and a round cap are added

check.describe: Five shapes on a dark background: blue filled rect, violet outlined rounded rect, teal disc, green outlined oval, red round-capped diagonal line. Resized, the whole drawing scales uniformly to fit and stays centred (smaller in a narrow box, centred with margins in a wide one).

pitfalls: Paint state persists between commands: after a stroke paint every shape is outlined until a paint sets style fill again (the circle does)
The paint starts as a solid fill, so the first shape needs only a colour
drawRect and drawOval take left/top/right/bottom edges, not x/y/width/height

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: literal coordinates sit in the top-left and get cut off when it is resized, so scale the drawing to fit (or derive positions from componentWidth()/componentHeight())
